transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-08-04 10:00 PDT | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Sara Lopez (Redwood SE), Ravi Patel (Mercury Health - Lead ML Eng), Laura Kim (Mercury - Head of Platform), Omar Nabil (Mercury - Infra)

Summary: quick bench review vs baseline provider, dig into p99 spikes and throughput.

00:00 Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um this is our weekly poc sync to go over the benchmark numbers we shared yesterday. Sara's gonna walk us through the results.
00:18 Sara: cool yeah hi team, uh quick context, we ran two sets, our Redwood Dedicated-like config on the pilot nodes and then the customer baseline provider run you shared from 7/31. We're comparing latency distributions and sustained throughput.
00:35 Ravi: quick question, the baseline run was on their managed endpoints with 4x A100s right? or was it 8x? the runbook said 4 but the 7/31 notes mentioned burst.
00:48 Laura: yeah it's 4 nodes with autoscale to 6 for spikes, but the steady-state is 4.
00:54 Sara: ok thanks; we tried to mirror the steady state. Highlights: average token latency was comparable, we were slightly better on median, but p95 and p99 showed some variance - p99 was about 1200ms for their baseline and 1400-1800ms on our initial runs depending on sequence length and batching.
01:14 Omar: that's the number that worries me, p99 going up, is that from network egress or model kernel choice?
01:21 Sara: good call. We instrumented traces and it looks like two contributors: prefix/KV cache misses on longer contexts and occasional GPU kernel fallback on longer sequences causing increased compute tail. There's also a small network jitter component because their baseline test was region-local and our pilot VPC had NAT egress via a different AZ.
01:42 Alex: right so two levers: software tuning (batching config, aggressive KV prefix caching, quantization profile to select the faster kernels) and infra (VPC peering or co-located infra to cut network jitter).
01:54 Ravi: can you remind me what quant profile you used for the Redwood run? I saw q4_0 in the artifact but not sure if that's the most aggressive.
02:03 Sara: we ran q4_0 for the baseline Redwood run to be conservative. We have a q4_1 and q3 mixed profiles that can reduce compute latency but with slightly different quality tradeoffs. Also there was a slight difference in effective batch sizes - their provider used larger multiplexing which helps throughput but sometimes hurts latency tails.
02:23 Laura: can you explain multiplexing vs batching in plain terms? for infra folks here.
02:28 Sara: sure - batching is assembling multiple requests into one GPU op at the same time, multiplexing is more like concurrency at the runtime where we interleave small requests across threads to keep GPU saturated. Batching increases throughput but can increase tail latency if you wait to collect enough requests; multiplexing keeps latency lower but uses kernel-level concurrency.
02:45 Omar: so is the plan to try a different tradeoff? improved throughput or lower p99?
02:50 Alex: depends on your SLOs - Ravi, you mentioned a 95th percentile SLA target in the deck right?
02:56 Ravi: we target p95 under 500ms for user-facing flows, p99 ideally under 900ms but we can tolerate a small fraction above in extreme bursts.
03:06 Sara: ok that explains priorities. For user-facing we should tune for lower p95/p99 even if throughput drops a bit - so we can test reduced batch wait time, enable more aggressive KV caching and try q4_1 to see kernel improvements.
03:18 Alex: we already did a quick head-to-head in the lab: with tighter batch wait (20ms) and q4_1 we shaved about 15% off p99 on mid-length contexts but throughput fell 8%. The baseline provider's larger multiplexing kept their throughput up while p99 was still native due to region locality.
03:36 Ravi: hmmm, region locality - can we co-locate the pilot with them? we can't replicate their exact infra but we can peer VPCs?
03:43 Laura: we'll need to look at peering and NAT egress, looks like the NAT in our pilot AZ added ~80-120ms jitter at times. If we peer or put Redwood nodes in our same AZ that should remove most network delta.
03:55 Sara: yes, recommend trying a peering test next run; we can also run a purely intra-AZ test.
04:02 Omar: there's also the question of tokenization and context lengths in your test harness, our production workload hits 8k often, were these runs 4k?
04:10 Sara: good catch - initial runs were 4k; we did one 8k run that showed p99 moved further up. We'll run a full 8k focused A/B to match production.
04:19 Alex: ok so immediate plan: 1) re-run matched 8k A/B with peered infra, 2) test q4_1 and reduced batch wait, 3) capture raw traces and logs and share. Anything else?
04:31 Ravi: can you share the kernel selection notes and quant profiles so our team can audit quality delta?
04:36 Sara: yep will share docs and the eval samples we used, plus the prompt sets.
04:41 Laura: what's the timeline for those runs?
04:43 Alex: we can run the A/B this week, aim to have data by Friday. Sara, you good to own?
04:50 Sara: yes I'll own re-run, I'll need the peering from Laura's infra team by Wednesday to do intra-AZ tests.
04:58 Laura: we'll try to enable peering by Tuesday EOD.
05:02 Alex: great. Two other items - security/compliance: Ravi asked for SOC2 docs and audit log retention details. We already uploaded an initial pack to the shared drive but I'll drop direct links and the SOC2 summary.
05:14 Ravi: perfect, also can you confirm encryption change management and KMS integration?
05:19 Alex: yes Redwood supports customer KMS and HSM integrations on Private; for the pilot we have envelope encryption with customer-managed keys - Sara will include config notes.
05:29 Sara: quick note on observation - we saw one outlier in the 7/31 run that looked like a kernel fallback to a slower path, likely due to sequence length crossing a threshold which triggered a different kernel schedule. We'll add kernel time-series to the next logs.
05:45 Omar: that would help. Also can you surface GPU utilization traces at the same timestamps so we can correlate?
05:51 Sara: yes will include utilization and per-kernel timings.
05:56 Alex: ok great. Any blockers on the run?
05:58 Ravi: none, just need the peering and the baseline logs.
06:02 Laura: we'll share peering details and try to get NAT removal done.
06:07 Alex: perfect. Recap of next steps - Alex to run A/B, Sara to provide quant docs, Laura to enable peering, Ravi to share baseline logs, and exchange pricing delta after re-run. We'll reconvene next Monday same time unless we need a mid-week deep dive.
06:24 Ravi: sounds good, thanks everyone.
06:27 Alex: thanks all, meeting adjourned.
